correctness.rationale: With C_k the coefficient of e^(ikt) in the intensity, each k=2n−j>n has only the term b·conj(a_j), recovering the head even if it contains zeros. At smaller positive lags, subtract the fixed head products; the data for z=a_n are conj(a_(n−k))z for k<n and conj(a_0)z+b·conj(z) at k=n. The squared change on a perturbation h is S|h|²+|conj(a_0)h+b·conj(h)|². On the unit circle the cross term ranges over its full phase, so the claimed squared extremes are attained, including when a_0=0 or the middle is empty. At rank loss, S=0 and |a_0|=|b|. Rotate z by a unit square root of b/conj(a_0); the remaining positive lag fixes the rotated real part and C_0 fixes the modulus. Exactly the stated reflected pair results, possibly coincident. On the full sequence this is conjugate reversal times the unique phase preserving b and a_0. A 4n+1 grid separates the Fourier modes −2n through 2n. With m≥2n+1 every reference-to-unknown lag exceeds n and separates. All arguments include n=1.
residual_risks: The Lipschitz constants are for the forward nonzero positive-lag map with fixed head. On its injective stratum the inverse's constants are reciprocal and reversed; this is not an end-to-end noise bound. The grid count is sufficient only. The checker exercises finite cases, and its expected terminal line is not evidence of independent replay.
